input:
The staffing ramp for the upgrade project has been set at 16%, and this section sets out the reasoning behind that figure and the reasons why a lower alternative has not been adopted. A lower ramp was considered during the preparation of the proposal, but it was felt that a lower figure would leave the project exposed during the period in which the workload rises most steeply, since the work that the ramp is intended to cover does not arrive evenly and cannot readily be deferred. The costs that correspond to the ramp are set out in the cost table in the Costs section, to which the reader is referred for the underlying figures, which are not repeated here.

The steering group has reviewed the basis of the ramp and the alternative that was put to it, and the figure stated here is the figure that will be carried forward to FID unless the steering group directs otherwise. It should be noted that the ramp is a planning allowance rather than a commitment to a particular pattern of appointments, and its purpose is to ensure that the upgrade project is not placed in the position of having to recruit at short notice against a fixed programme.
target:
The staffing ramp for the upgrade project is set at 16%. A lower alternative was considered and set aside: the work the ramp covers does not arrive evenly, and the steepest rise falls early, when posts left unfilled cannot be recovered by later hiring against a fixed programme. A ramp sized on the average load fails in the period that sets the programme. Recruitment also runs behind the decision that authorises it: a post approved at the start of a quarter is filled later in the programme than the approval date suggests, and the ramp carries that lag as well as the workload itself. The costs of the ramp stand in the cost table in the Costs section and are not repeated here.

The steering group has reviewed the figure and the alternative, and this ramp is the figure carried forward to FID. The ramp is a planning allowance, not a commitment to a pattern of appointments. Its function is narrower than recruitment itself: it holds the resource line at the level the programme requires, so that the upgrade project does not recruit at short notice against dates that cannot move.
